subject.title: [Feature]: Add Korean (ko) language support to Control UI and AI agent

question: Should OpenClaw add a global agent response-language persistence rule and automatic Korean-aware search defaults, or leave language continuity to existing compaction/custom-instruction mechanisms unless a narrower failing transcript proves a runtime bug?
rationale: The UI locale request is already implemented, while the remaining agent/search behavior changes core prompt and provider-tool policy in ways that need maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Split and require proof
options.body: Keep this issue open only for a narrower maintainer-approved agent/search policy follow-up, with a redacted Korean transcript and focused tests before code changes.

options.title: Adopt global language policy
options.body: Explicitly sponsor a global same-language response rule and provider-aware search-language defaults, accepting the mixed-language and provider-semantics tradeoffs.

options.title: Close as UI satisfied
options.body: Decide that shipped UI localization plus compaction-summary preservation is enough, and close without adding general agent/search policy.

recommendation.title: Split and require proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open only for a narrower maintainer-approved agent/search policy follow-up, with a redacted Korean transcript and focused tests before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent closed the paired mixed-scope PR and has direct history on the generated Control UI locale path, making him the best observed owner for deciding how much of the remaining scope belongs in core.
